_provenance: PROVENANCE AND ACCURACY — read before trusting this file.
These entries were AUTHORED from general knowledge of brands and pack
sizes commonly sold in Kuwait. They were NOT scraped, and they were NOT
checked against any retailer's live inventory: the approved Phase 0
decision is a human-curated catalogue with Sharq Coop and Deliveroo
Kuwait as reference sources only (master plan Section 5A,
docs/architecture/14-technical-risks-decisions.md item 6).
So treat this as a realistic STARTING POINT that a person should verify
in-store or against a retailer's own listing, not as verified fact. A
brand may have left the market, a pack size may be wrong, and an item
may not be stocked by the specific co-op a household shops at.
NO PRICES. Not omitted by convention — the products table has no price
column at all, and the importer refuses any file containing one.
source_name is left null because these were not taken from a specific
retailer listing. When an entry IS verified against one, set source_name
and image_source_url on that row so the provenance is per-row rather
than assumed for the whole file.
image_url is null throughout: no third-party product images are
re-hosted (master plan Section 5). The UI falls back to the category
icon until owned or licensed photography exists.
`type` references a key in product-types.json, which carries the nine
localized names. `unit` here overrides the type's default only when the
pack differs.
2026-08 — FRUIT EXPANSION. Fruits & Vegetables grew from 24 entries to
40: sixteen fruits were added (green apple, red grapes, mandarin, lime,
strawberry, blueberries, raspberry, cherry, peach, plum, pear, kiwi,
pineapple, pomegranate, avocado, cantaloupe), and two existing generic
entries were made specific to match the photography that now backs them
-- `apple` is Red Apples and `grapes` is Green Grapes, each with its
colour counterpart as a separate entry.
These 24 fruits are the first rows in the catalogue to carry real
product photography, supplied by the owner as licensed stock and
converted to web-sized .webp by the images pipeline. They are also the
first rows translated into all TWELVE app languages rather than nine:
name_am / name_fr / name_fon are nullable columns
(20260812180000_catalog_12_languages.sql), so the remaining 152 product
types still fall back to English in those three until they are reached.
TRANSLATION QUALITY, same caveat as the original nine: the Amharic,
French and Fon fruit names were authored without native-speaker review.
French is low-risk; Fon is the most likely to need correction, since
several of these fruits have no settled Fon term and the entries lean on
borrowings. Fixing one is an edit to product-types.json plus a re-run of
the importer -- no schema change, no redeploy.
2026-08 — ONE PRODUCT PER TYPE. The catalogue previously carried
brand+size variants: 311 rows for 184 types, so browsing Dairy showed
six Fresh Milk tiles that differed only by a brand name and a pack
size. The owner's requirement is the opposite -- one 'Milk', one
'Yogurt', one 'Cream' -- with anything more specific written as the
optional note on the list item ('lactose-free', '2 litre'), which is
what shopping_list_items.note has existed for since Phase 6.
So `brand` and `size` are no longer set by this file, natural_key is
just '<type>||', and the products table is a vocabulary of THINGS
rather than of shelf SKUs. The columns remain in the schema: they cost
nothing empty, and a future 'preferred brand' feature would want them
back rather than a migration to re-add them.
